subject: Math
prompt:
Which of the following ordered pairs $(x, y)$ satisfies the inequality $y \le -2x + 6$?

I. $(1, 3)$

II. $(2, 4)$

III. $(-1, 7)$
explanation: Testing point I: $(1, 3)$. Substituting gives $3 \leq -2(1) + 6$, or $3 \leq 4$, which is true. Testing point II: $(2, 4)$. Substituting gives $4 \leq -2(2) + 6$, or $4 \leq 2$, which is false. Testing point III: $(-1, 7)$. Substituting gives $7 \leq -2(-1) + 6$, or $7 \leq 8$, which is true. Therefore, only I and III satisfy the inequality.
